deepdive.sec: Financial Services — NBFC (Vehicle Finance: new/used 2-Wheeler, 3-Wheeler, used car, MSME-LAP, top-up)

bull_bear.body: CAR 24.46%, comfortably above regulatory minimum; management comfortable operating up to ~4x debt-to-equity. Declared interim dividend of 7.5% (face value ₹10) during the year plus a recommended final dividend of 2.5% (subject to shareholder approval) — continued small but explicit dividend payout alongside growth capital needs. Planned equity raise (flagged in a prior call) pushed from Q2/Q3 to Q3/Q4 (calendar) given a depressed share price; management explicitly linked raise timing to price recovery (targeting ~₹135-150) rather than committing to a fixed date regardless of valuation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- AUM-guidance inconsistency (25-30% stated philosophy vs. ₹2,300-2,400cr FY27 implied ~34-40% growth) — reconcile next quarter.
- Equity-raise timing already slipped once; a further macro-driven (unspecified geopolitical/"war situation") stock-price weakness could push it out again, keeping leverage/capital-growth funding reliant on debt in the interim.
- 3-Wheeler EV financing flagged by management itself as "very, very challenging" (fast depreciation, RTO overloading/misuse) — deliberately slow-paced and OEM-selective; a scale-up beyond current comfort would be a watch-item.
- Small business loan (unsecured, <5% of AUM) showing rising rejection ratio — a soft early signal of caution on the unsecured sliver of the book, though management stresses no broader stress observed yet (fuel-price/macro question from an analyst was explicitly addressed).
- New-geography (UP/MP) expansion being run at lower yields (18-19% vs 21-22%) to protect asset quality — margin/growth trade-off to monitor as these states scale.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, granular, and generally transparent — MD volunteered specific portfolio-mix trajectories (2W 84%→60-65% in 3 years), named exact OEM tie-ups and even acknowledged a stock-price-driven equity-raise delay candidly rather than deflecting. One area of imprecision: credit-cost figures were quoted inconsistently across the call (headline "~1%" vs. a corrected "1.12%" vs. partial pushback on an analyst's +25bps observation) — a minor tone flag on numerical discipline in Q&A, not a red flag on substance.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Management's own AUM math doesn't tie out: "25-30% growth" repeated as philosophy, but the explicit FY27 AUM target (₹2,300-2,400cr) implies a materially higher ~34-40% growth off the ₹1,713-1,718cr FY26 base — flag for verification next quarter (either the growth-rate language or the absolute target is stale).
- The equity-raise delay is explicitly priced off Manba's own stock (targeting ₹135-150 vs. current levels), not off a fixed calendar or capital need — meaning the raise is optionally-timed to valuation recovery, a nuance for anyone modeling near-term dilution/capital events.
- TVS Motor relationship is sourcing-only for now — an analyst asked directly about TVS taking an equity stake (drawing the parallel to TVS Group's investment in Jana Small Finance Bank); management explicitly denied any such discussion at this stage.
- PCR was raised in a profitable year specifically to "strengthen the balance sheet" pre-emptively against unspecified future shocks ("any kind of natural calamity or anything") — a conservative signal, not a response to observed deterioration.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital Adequacy Ratio of 24.40% (Q1-FY27), with the trend shown as FY24 24.56%, FY25 29.81%, FY26 24.46%, Q1-FY27 24.40%; Debt Equity Ratio stated at 3.44.
- 'Raised INR 6.5 Bn through Non-Convertible Debentures over the last two years at the rate of 10.5% ROI.'
- Borrowings distribution (INR Mn) shown for FY24 / FY25 / FY26 / Q1-FY27 as Secured Term Loans 4,167 / 6,468 / 8,576 / 8,316; NCD 1,626 / 2,388 / 4,843 / 4,515; Others 1,748 / 1,894 / 2,117 / 1,738; funding sources are labelled Bank, SFB and NBFC.
- Provision Coverage Ratio of 26.00% (Q1-FY27), with the trend shown as FY24 20.00%, FY25 24.00%, FY26 26.00%, Q1-FY27 26.00%.
- Return metrics based on FY26 financials: Return on Equity 11.65% and Return on Asset 2.63%; the ROE trend shown is FY24 15.55%, FY25 10.25%, FY26 11.65% and ROA FY24 3.20%, FY25 2.58%, FY26 2.63%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **2-Wheeler (84.5% of portfolio)**: new-2W ticket size ₹80,000-85,000, yield ~21%; used-2W ticket size ₹55,000-60,000, yield ~24-26%, LTV ~50-55%; used-2W NPA experience so far "promising," expected ~1-1.5-2% max credit loss.
- **3-Wheeler (3.28%)**: ~₹50cr book, of which ~₹40cr is EV; funding intentionally slow/select-OEM-only given depreciation/misuse risk (RTO permit overloading cited as a specific risk driver); two OEM MOUs now provide ~50% loss-sharing on POS outstanding at NPA/seizure, giving management comfort to become "a little aggressive" here.
- **Used car**: separate sales/credit/collection teams; ticket size ~₹4 lakh (vs ₹80k for 2W); turnaround time ~3 hours (vs 1-minute 2W sanction).
- **Small business loan (4.93%, unsecured)**: rejection ratio rising, growth being deliberately throttled — the only unsecured product, capped at <5% of AUM.
- **MSME LAP (new)**: 2 branches live (Mumbai, Pune), gross yield ~18-19% (secured, LTV up to ~60%), ticket size ₹5-20 lakh; hiring (RAs/business managers/BCM) complete at both branches, disbursement started with good response.
- **EV 2-Wheeler**: ~7-8% of portfolio (in line with industry mix); NPA <1% after ~3.5 years of financing, attributed to more "informed"/economy-focused, educated customer profile; focus OEMs: TVS iQube, Bajaj Chetak, Ather.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Turnaround time: >60% of 2W loans sanctioned within one minute, 92% within a day — cited as an industry-leading speed differentiator that drives dealer preference.
- Collection-driven underwriting culture: management repeatedly ties low NPA to an internal collection team + calibrated new-geography pricing (lending 18-19% vs 21-22% in new geographies to select better-quality customers upfront) rather than to any external guarantee/insurance structure.
- EV 2W book NPA <1% after 3.5+ years — an evidenced (not merely asserted) track record, differentiated by customer-profile selection (informed/educated buyers) rather than product structure.

business.body:
- Described as an NBFC providing tailored financial solutions for two wheelers, three wheelers, used cars, MSME LAP loans and personal loans, with AUM of INR 17,308 Mn of which the snapshot states '95% Secured AUM'; the Company Overview separately states 'Almost 100% of loans given are under secured credit exposure' (both readings appear in the deck).
- Four stated structural differentiators ('What Sets Manba Apart'): lower cost to collect (6% vs 18%), security at the core (95% of AUM secured), quick loans (60% approved within one minute, 92% within a single day) and diversifying beyond the core.
- Claims 'one of the fastest turnaround times for loan sanctions in the industry, with over 60% loans sanctioned in 1-minute and 92% loans in 1 day' and asserts 'Lowest NPAs in the industry.'
- Credit ratings stated as CARE BBB+ (Positive Outlook) and ACUITE A-.
- Positioned around new-to-credit borrowers: '40% of the new loans are given to the new to credit people', 1 Million+ customers served, and '<1.5% Credit Less, despite serving underserved segments' (deck's own wording).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Co-lending / partnerships] Deck cites Muthoot co-lending (2023), a TVS Motor pan-India 3W MoU (2025) and a Sreesastha (Nammaloan) partnership for the South India entry; State Bank of India is stated to have emerged as the largest lending partner in 2026.
- [Promoter / governance] Founded by Mr. Manish Shah, a first-generation entrepreneur, who is Managing Director; the board includes Whole Time Directors Nikita Manish Shah, Monil Manish Shah and Jay Khushal Mota (also CFO), with Nallepilly Ramaswami Parameswaran as Independent Director and Chairman alongside Independent Directors Sujay Jagani, Neelam Tater and Abhinav Sharma.
- [Market context, third-party sourced] Market sizing attributed to FADA Report, CRIF Highmark, Crisil Intelligence and ET BFSI: 2W financing market INR 1.60 Tn (FY25) to INR 2.50 Tn (FY28P); used cars financing market INR 1.07 Tn (FY25) to INR 1.71 Tn (FY28P); MSME credit gap of INR 25 Lakh Crore; FY26 units sold of 21.4 Mn two-wheelers, 1.4 Mn three-wheelers and 6.0 Mn used cars.
- [IR disclaimer] The presentation carries a Valorem Advisors disclaimer stating it was prepared by Valorem Advisors, an independent investor relations management service company.

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 13.63% FY26 on gross yield 22.85% — funding-cost tailwind (avg cost of borrowing 10.64%, down 16bps YoY; incremental cost down further to 10.50% from 11.25% a year ago) is the main margin driver, not pricing action.
- Company raised ₹1,265cr in FY26 (term loans ₹651cr, NCDs ₹365cr, balance via other instruments); Q4 alone ₹420cr including a ₹100cr SBI term-loan sanction at ~10% and a ₹50cr NCD, plus new lending relationships (Protium Finance, Godrej Finance, Godrej Housing Finance).
- Credit cost stable at ~1-1.25% (management gave slightly different figures across the call: "around 1%" headline vs. 1.12% precise FY26 figure vs. an analyst-flagged +25bps YoY that management partially pushed back on, landing on ~10bps increase) — worth reconciling against FY25 base next quarter.
- PCR deliberately raised from ~24% to ~26% this year — management frames this as balance-sheet strengthening during a profitable year, not a reaction to deteriorating asset quality.

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** First note for this company. AUM ₹1,713cr (+29% YoY), Q4 NII +34% YoY, Q4 PAT ₹11cr (+39% YoY); asset quality stable/improving (GNPA 3.33%, NNPA 2.46%); cost of borrowing falling (10.64% avg, 10.50% incremental); TVS Motor 3-Wheeler MOU ramping (70 dealers in 3 months); MSME LAP launched (2 branches); equity raise pushed to Q3/Q4 (calendar) on depressed stock price.
- _Q1 FY27 → check: Karnataka branch launch, MSME LAP expansion to Nashik/Ahmedabad, credit-cost reconciliation (headline vs. precise figures given this call), whether the ₹2,300-2,400cr FY27 AUM target vs. "25-30% growth" language gets reconciled, equity-raise timing/pricing, cost-of-borrowing trajectory (any further 20-50bps cuts realized), West Bengal entry decision._

outlook.body:
- AUM growth: management reiterated a "25-30% every year" philosophy but separately guided to ₹2,300-2,400cr for FY27 (implies ~34-40% growth off ₹1,713-1,718cr base) — an internal inconsistency to watch/reconcile.
- Portfolio mix: 2-Wheeler share to fall from 84.5% today to ~60-65% within 3 years as 3-Wheeler, used-vehicle, top-up, personal loan and MSME LAP scale up (in absolute ₹ terms 2W still grows, just a smaller % of a larger book).
- Geography: Karnataka launch targeted Q2 FY27; West Bengal under evaluation but "not immediately" — maybe by end of this year or into FY28. UP and MP flagged as under-penetrated (~1% and ~3% market share respectively) — key growth levers.
- MSME LAP: currently 2 branches (Mumbai, Pune); Nashik and Ahmedabad to open next quarter; targeted to be "very mature" and a meaningful secured, lower-credit-loss product within a year.
- Cost of borrowing: management pushing lenders for a further 20-50bps reduction each quarter; no further large step-down guided given "external situation."
- Equity fundraise: previously guided for Q2/Q3 (calendar) window, now pushed to Q3/Q4 given depressed stock price (traded ₹140-150 in Feb-2026 before an unspecified geopolitical/"war situation" hit the price); management wants price back near ₹135-150 before raising. Comfortable leverage ceiling: debt-to-equity below 4x.
- No explicit margin/NIM guidance given for FY27 beyond directional commentary on falling cost of funds.

deepdive.thesis: Manba delivered a clean Q4/FY26 beat with AUM at ₹1,713cr (+29% YoY), NII +34% YoY in Q4 and PAT +39% YoY in Q4 (₹11cr), on stable asset quality (GNPA 3.33%, NNPA 2.46%, credit cost ~1-1.25%) and a falling cost of borrowing (10.64% avg, incremental now 10.50%); management guides 25-30%+ AUM growth via geographic diversification (UP/MP/Karnataka), product diversification (MSME LAP, used-2W, 3W-EV via TVS MOU) away from 2-Wheeler concentration (84.5% today → targeted 60-65% in 3 years) — but a planned equity raise has been pushed out a couple of quarters given a depressed stock price blamed on an unspecified "geopolitical/war situation."
